description: LSM-tree internals decomposed. RocksDB / LevelDB / Cassandra / HBase architecture. MemTable + immutable memtable + WAL + L0...Ln SSTables. Leveled vs tiered compaction. Bloom filters. Block cache. Read/write/space amplification trade-offs.

sub_mechanisms.name: active_memtable
sub_mechanisms.definition: In-memory writable structure. Concurrent skip list typical. Sorted; supports point + range queries.
sub_mechanisms.why: Fast in-memory writes. Skip list permits concurrent insertion without locks. Size-bounded; flushed to L0 SSTable when full.

sub_mechanisms.name: immutable_memtable
sub_mechanisms.definition: When active memtable fills, becomes immutable + new active created. Background thread flushes immutable to L0.
sub_mechanisms.why: Decouples write absorption from flush. Active memtable always accepts writes; flushes happen async. Pause-free behaviour for write path.

sub_mechanisms.name: L0_SSTables
sub_mechanisms.definition: Level 0: flush output. SSTables here may overlap in key ranges (each flush is independent).
sub_mechanisms.why: Direct memtable flush. Reads must check all L0 SSTables (overlap). Bloom filters per SSTable filter out misses. L0 → L1 compaction merges + sorts.

sub_mechanisms.name: leveled_compaction
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each level Ln has non-overlapping SSTables. Compacting Ln file picks overlapping Ln+1 files; merges into new Ln+1 files.
sub_mechanisms.why: Tight read amplification: each level contributes ≤ 1 SSTable to check. Cost: write amplification ~10x (each level's data rewritten). RocksDB default for read-heavy workloads.

sub_mechanisms.name: tiered_compaction
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each level has multiple SSTables (potentially overlapping). Compaction triggers when N similar-sized SSTables accumulate.
sub_mechanisms.why: Lower write amplification (~3x vs 10x). Cost: higher read amplification + space amplification. Used in Cassandra default, RocksDB for write-heavy workloads.

sub_mechanisms.name: compaction_priority
sub_mechanisms.definition: Decides which SSTables to compact next. Strategies: oldest first, smallest first, file age.
sub_mechanisms.why: Affects how compaction debt accumulates. Bad choice = compaction lag = ballooning read amp. RocksDB exposes pluggable strategies.

sub_mechanisms.name: tombstone
sub_mechanisms.definition: Deletion marker. DELETE inserts a tombstone; reads return 'not found'. Tombstones removed during compaction.
sub_mechanisms.why: LSM can't physically delete in-place. Tombstones propagate through compaction. Long-lived tombstones (range deletes) hurt performance — read paths must skip them.

sub_mechanisms.name: block_cache
sub_mechanisms.definition: In-memory cache of recently-read SSTable blocks (typically 4-64 KB). LRU + optional pinning.
sub_mechanisms.why: Hot data stays in memory. RocksDB's BlockBasedTable has block cache + index cache + filter cache. Hit rate dominates read performance.

sub_mechanisms.name: level_size_multiplier
sub_mechanisms.definition: Ln target size = L0 size × multiplier^n. Typically 10x. Caps tree depth + bounds read amp.
sub_mechanisms.why: Geometric level growth: 64 MB L0, 640 MB L1, 6.4 GB L2, etc. Caps levels logarithmically. RocksDB tunable; default 10.

sub_mechanisms.name: bloom_filter_per_sstable
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-SSTable bloom filter. ~10 bits per key gives <1% false positive.
sub_mechanisms.why: Critical for read performance. Each SSTable lookup first checks bloom; skip if 'definitely not present'. Without, every read would touch every SSTable.

sub_mechanisms.name: merge_iterator
sub_mechanisms.definition: Read path: heap-merge iterators over memtable + each SSTable. Returns next key from any source.
sub_mechanisms.why: Range queries traverse all sources simultaneously. Heap ensures correct order. Latest version wins on duplicate keys.

sub_mechanisms.name: manifest_log
sub_mechanisms.definition: Persistent log of SSTable additions + deletions + level metadata. Recovers consistent state on restart.
sub_mechanisms.why: Tracks which SSTables exist. Crash safety: replay manifest to find current state. Without it, restart would need to scan all files.

derivation_rules.name: LSM_optimises_writes_at_read_cost
if: all writes are append + sequential flush
then: write throughput maximised but read may check multiple files
derivation_rules.why: Sequential writes are fast (no seeks). LSM never updates in place. Cost: reads check memtable + L0 + L1...Ln. Bloom filters + compaction keep read amp bounded.

derivation_rules.name: leveled_vs_tiered_trades_WA_for_RA_SA
derivation_rules.why: Tiered: write each level data fewer times. Leveled: each level data rewritten ~10x. Read penalty: tiered has more files per level → more bloom checks. Pick based on workload mix.

derivation_rules.name: bloom_filter_essential_for_LSM_reads
if: bloom filters per SSTable are absent or poorly tuned
then: read amplification grows linearly with SSTable count
derivation_rules.why: Without bloom: read must check every SSTable's index. With 10 SSTables, 10x cost. With bloom: 'not present' eliminates most before index lookup. Bloom is the difference between viable + unviable LSM.

derivation_rules.name: tombstone_lifetime_affects_query_performance
then: range queries pay cost to skip them
derivation_rules.why: Each tombstone in the merge iterator must be traversed. Long-lived tombstones (haven't compacted away) accumulate. Cassandra's range delete is famous performance gotcha.

derivation_rules.name: level_size_multiplier_bounds_depth
if: each level is M times the previous
derivation_rules.why: M=10, total=100GB, L0=64MB → ~3 levels. Geometric levels bound depth logarithmically. Read amp = O(levels) = O(log total_size). RocksDB default makes 10-level trees rare.
